statement: You receive a row of integers. Sort it into ascending order with bubble sort written recursively: one call performs a single left-to-right sweep that swaps out-of-order neighbours, parking the largest value of the current range at its end; the call then recurses on the range that is one shorter. A range of one value is the base case. Print the sorted values on one line, separated by single spaces.

example.why: Sweep one parks 9, the recursive call on the first three parks 7, and so on down to one value.

hint: The recursion mirrors the outer loop of the iterative version; the sweep is the same code either way.
mistake: Recursing on the same length after a sweep - the recursion must shrink the range or it never reaches the base case.
